nodes.label: The modified-sine-wave-destroys-your-PSU claim is a vendor risk-mitigation narrative, with no defect bulletin, teardown, or reproducible test behind it; the documented failure is the PC shutting itself off on transfer

nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - riset-dukungan-ups-di-linux [ses_f18de69a7ffeh5014GS0F4Adgz].md:L11851] Pure sine wave exists at 1000-1500 VA from CyberPower for roughly the price of a 650 VA stepped-sine unit, which makes it cheap insurance for an APFC PSU

nodes.label: The ATX 17 ms hold-up figure is specified at 100% of rated load, so a 100 W system on a 500 W PSU has several times that margin and a 10 ms UPS transfer is not the problem
nodes.norm_label: atx 17 ms hold up is a full load figure
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - riset-dukungan-ups-di-linux [ses_f18de69a7ffeh5014GS0F4Adgz].md:L11876] Transfer time is not the risk because hold-up scales with capacitor energy over power, so at a fifth of rated load the margin is 3-5x; the real risk is hold-up degradation from aged bulk capacitors, and the waveform is a separate smaller risk
